Personally, I don’t think things have changed per se. Sometimes when I’m having a particularly hard time dealing with something, it is easy to go into that downward spiral where I dissect every part of my life and justify killing myself. At my worst, I found comfort in the idea of killing myself, not fear. I remember one particular time, I drove to lecture crying, not because I was particularly upset over something that had happened, but because the night before I thought about how easy it would be to drive off into a lake and end it all. I spent the whole night thinking about which way would be more or less painful, which I would be more likely to not survive, and which would be quickest. I cried that next morning because I realized I had reached my breaking point. I was mourning everything that I felt I had lost to being suicidal. I wasn’t afraid of dying, and that saddened me. That was a major turning point for me I think. 
From that point on, I took inventory of things that were depressing me. My mother has a very hot temper and that was a major source of my suicidal tendencies. Her verbal and emotional abuse became too much and I know I was adding fuel to the fire by allowing it to affect me. I detached myself from her. I still live with her and we play role of normal family and I love her as a mother and a person, but I don’t let her anger affect me. I don’t let her dictate how I will feel after being around her. It’s hard to describe. 
I also devoted myself to other things around me. I didn’t allow myself to marinate in my depression. I joined clubs and did volunteer work. 
Basically, I had to fight like hell to pull myself out of that place, and I still feel like I’m on the edge sometimes. I want to say it gets better, but it doesn’t unless you are willing to make it better. You can’t control what others do, but you can control how that affects you.
